Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

G=load()
T=G['Test input']
def solve(g, mode):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    P=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if g[i][j]==4]
    AX=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if g[i][j]==6]
    pm=max(i for i,_ in P); pc=min(j for _,j in P); mc=max(j for _,j in P)
    out=[r[:] for r in g]
    for i,j in AX: out[i][j]=0
    if mode=='left':
        for i,j in P: out[i][pc-1-(j-pc)]=4
    elif mode=='right':
        for i,j in P: out[i][2*mc+1-j]=4
    return out
# D3 anchor right of pattern bbox (acols 5-7 > 3) but copy on right. D4 anchor left (acols1-3<4) copy on right. So H-case -> always RIGHT? Check with demos: D3 copy cols 4-6 (right), D4 copy cols 7-9 (right). Yes both right! And V-case -> always BELOW (demos 1,2). Simple unified rule: vertical flip below OR horizontal flip right, based on column-overlap of anchor.
def f(g):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    P=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if g[i][j]==4]
    AX=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if g[i][j]==6]
    acols={j for _,j in AX}; pcols={j for _,j in P}
    pm=max(i for i,_ in P); mc=max(j for _,j in P); pc=min(j for _,j in P)
    out=[r[:] for r in g]
    for i,j in AX: out[i][j]=0
    if acols & pcols:
        for i,j in P: out[2*pm+1-i][j]=4
    else:
        for i,j in P: out[i][2*mc+1-j]=4

G=load(); pairs={n:(G[n+' input'],G[n+' output']) for n in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2','Demo pair 3','Demo pair 4','Demo pair 5']}
# Demo 5: pattern rows4-6 cols3-8; anchor rows8-10 cols8-11 (mostly BELOW and slightly right). Copy: V-flip ABOVE pattern, axis y=3.5 (= pattern top - 0.5).
# So the side of the copy depends on the anchor's quadrant! Let me tabulate: which copy-side was chosen and where the anchor sits relative to the pattern bbox.
def info(n):
    gi,go=G[n+' input'],G[n+' output']
    h,w=len(gi),len(gi[0])
    P=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if gi[i][j]==4]
    AX=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if gi[i][j]==6]
    pr,pm=min(i for i,_ in P),max(i for i,_ in P); pc,mc=min(j for _,j in P),max(j for _,j in P)
    ar,am=min(i for i,_ in AX),max(i for i,_ in AX); ac,amc=min(j for _,j in AX),max(j for _,j in AX)
    return (P,AX),(pr,pm,pc,mc),(ar,am,ac,amc)
for n in pairs:
    (P,AX),(pr,pm,pc,mc),(ar,am,ac,amc)=info(n)
    print(n,'pat',(pr,pm),'cols',(pc,mc),'anchor',(ar,am),(ac,amc))

G=load()
def blocks(n):
    gi,go=G[n+' input'],G[n+' output']
    h,w=len(gi),len(gi[0])
    return gi,go,h,w
for n,(gi,go) in pairs.items():
    h,w=len(gi),len(gi[0])
    P=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if gi[i][j]==4]
    Sp=set(P); A={(a,b) for a in range(h) for b in range(w) if gi[a][b]==6}
    AD={(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if go[i][j]==4 and gi[i][j]==0}
    pr=min(i for i,_ in P); pm=max(i for i,_ in P); pc=min(j for _,j in P); mc=max(j for _,j in P)
    ar=min(i for i,_ in A); am=max(i for i,_ in A); ac=min(j for _,j in A); anc=max(j for _,j in A)
    # does pattern touch border? distance of anchor from nearest border
    print(n,'h,w',h,w,'pad dist T',pr,'B',pm,'L',pc,'R',mc,'|A',(ar,am),(ac,anc))

    P=set((i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if gi[i][j]==4)
    A={(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if gi[i][j]==6}
    AD={(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if go[i][j]==4 and gi[i][j]==0}
    # is copy mirrored or identical? compare orientation: normalize both sets and check flipV, flipH membership
    def norm(S): return sorted((min(i for i,_ in S)-i0, j-min(j for _,j in S)) for i,j in S) if False else None
    mi=min(i for i,_ in P); mc0=min(j for _,j in P)
    pn=sorted((i-mi,j-mc0) for i,j in P)
    mi2=min(i for i,_ in AD); mc1=min(j for _,j in AD)
    an=sorted((i-mi2,j-mc1) for i,j in AD)
    same = an==pn
    print(n,'orientation same:',same)
